chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man when he is emancipated: is it for him to place himself wherever he wishes and to take as guardian whom he loves? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he is emancipated for the Sake of Allah, he is a slave of the one who emancipated him. So when he is emancipated and is made a freed slave (sa'ibah), then for him is that he places himself wherever he wishes and takes as guardian whom he wishes.'

key_terms.سَائِبَةً: A freed slave who is free from obligation to the master (sa'ibah)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in guardianship rights between a slave emancipated for God's sake versus one made a sa'ibah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between 'itq li-lahi' (emancipation for God's sake, where the master retains the right of guardianship as a form of gratitude) and 'sa'ibah' (unconditional emancipation, granting full autonomy). In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that the master's right to 'wilayah' is not inherent but derived from the specific mode of manumission, reflecting the merciful intent behind freeing slaves for God's sake.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam,f rom Aban, from Ismail Bin Al Fazal who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man when is emancipated, is it for him that he places himself wherever he so desires to, and makes a guardian to the one whom he loves to?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he is emancipated for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so he is a slave of the one who emancipated him. So when he is emancipated and is made a freed slave, so for him is that he places himself wherever he so desires to and makes a guardian the one who he so desires to’.
